Subject: PO requirements / invoice cadence for Redwood — follow up

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week — NovaWell's procurement team is lining up the legal and finance checklist. A few items we need confirmation on before we finalize the PO: 

- PO header fields: we require a vendor tax ID and a vendor remit ID (both shown on the attached NovaWell_PO_Template.pdf). Can you confirm the exact values Redwood would populate?
- Invoice cadence: by default our ERP prefers weekly invoice runs for usage-based vendors, but we're open to a monthly statement if you require it for licensing reasons. Does Redwood support weekly invoice statements for metered usage?
- Net terms: our standard is net45. Is Redwood able to accept net45 on the committed-reserved (Dedicated) contract?
- Discount eligibility: we have a multi-entity purchasing program. If we split the commitment across two legal entities, does that affect the discount slab or aggregation for volume tiers?

Also attaching our PO template for your legal/finance intake. Can you get back to us by Friday with a short answer on these so I can move to signature?

Thanks,
Lily Zhang
Procurement Manager
NovaWell Health

Hi Lily — thanks for the clear list and the template. Looping in Ben (billing) and Vanessa (enterprise sales ops) to confirm exact values and discount behavior. Quick answers below — I’ll follow up with specifics and the completed SOW by Friday.

- Vendor tax ID / remit: Redwood will provide the vendor TIN and preferred remit account; Ben will confirm the remit ID and the address we put on invoices.
- Weekly invoice runs: we do support weekly invoice statements for usage-based contracts on Dedicated — there are a couple of caveats around minimum invoice thresholds and batching. Ben, can you confirm the minimum weekly invoice amount and whether weekly runs create any reconciliation lag?
- Net45 on Dedicated: Vanessa — the standard is net30 on self-serve hosted, but net45 is doable on an enterprise Dedicated contract with an approved credit profile. We’ll need the legal entity and AP contact; we'll route for finance approval.
- Multi-entity discounting: Ben / Vanessa — does splitting the commitment across two entities break aggregation for discount slabs, or can we pool?

Action items:
1) Ben to confirm remit values, weekly invoice minimum and reconciliation impact.
2) Vanessa to confirm discount aggregation policy and next steps for net45 approval.
3) Monica to return signed SOW and annotated PO template once finance confirms.

Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: PO requirements / invoice cadence for Redwood — follow up

Monica — quick billing notes below for the PO template and weekly invoicing: 

- Vendor remit/TIN: Redwood TIN: 12-3456789; remit account: REDWOOD-AP-001; remit address: 2100 3rd St, San Francisco, CA 94107. Use the Redwood_SOW_v2.docx for SOW reference.
- Weekly invoice runs: Supported. Minimum invoice threshold for a weekly run is $1,200 USD to avoid micro-invoices. If spending for a given week is below that, we roll charges into the next weekly statement. That is configurable at onboarding but requires an ops flag for the billing system. Weekly runs may add a 1–2 business day reconciliation window for usage corrections (we provide mid-cycle correction credits).
- Net45 impact: Net45 increases DSO; finance requires a credit request form and a PO ledger sample before approving. Typical turnaround is 5–7 business days.
- Multi-entity discounting: Discounts are applied at the legal entity level by default. We can offer aggregation for customers that provide an intercompany agreement and consolidated billing mandate; that needs finance sign-off.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_v2.docx

If Lily confirms weekly runs and sends the PO with the remit ID, we can spin up the billing account and enable the weekly frequency.

—Ben
Director, Billing Operations
